newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices end up 1/4 to 3/8.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices end up 1/4 to 3/8.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices ended up 1/4 to 3/8 of a point or more amid bigger U.S. Treasury market gains and "very targeted" customer buying.

"(Munis are) trying to do a little bit better here on the heels of govies, but again, I think buyers are trying to have their way," one trader said. "They want to be able to get the structure and the price they want. It's kind of patient buying going on."
A municipal analyst said high-grade issues ended Thursday's session two basis points stronger overall.
The long end saw greater firming with yields improving by three basis points, the analyst said. Dollar bond prices ended up 3/8 of a point. Activity was light to moderate.
The trader cited limited cash and a desire to "tweak" portfolios as contributing to buyer pickiness.

"In order to tweak, they have to buy what they need, not necessarily because it's cheap or whatever," he said. "The market has been rallying here, and if they bought par bonds recently, now they are pricing to the call."
With their duration shortened, such buyers are likely looking for longer bonds, he said.

"A handful" of bid lists circulated, but "nothing of great consequence," the trader said. Franklin had about $15 million Metropolitan Pier & Exposition Authority bonds out, he said, adding, however, that most of Thursday's fare was substantially smaller.

In the government market, the benchmark 30-year bond closed up 24/32 at 99-11/32 to yield 6.80 percent. Economic data on weekly jobless claims, September housing starts and from the Philadelphia Federal Reserves' October business index reflected more economic weakness than expected.
Industrial production came in slightly higher than expected in September, but the rise was insufficient to unnerve the market.
In debt futures, the December municipal contract was up 18/32 at 114-26/32. The December T-bond contract was up 26/32 at 111-4/32. The MOB spread was 118 ticks.

As for new issues, an analyst described pricing as "firm." In negotiated action, PaineWebber Inc repriced and restructured $361 million New York City Municipal Water Finance Authority water and sewer system revenue bonds, cutting the yield in 2026 to 5.801 percent from 5.85 percent.

Elsewhere, Bear Stearns & Co repriced the Dormitory Authority of the State of New York's $87.9 million bond deal for St. John's University. Yields were lowered in several maturities and the top yield in 2026 was trimmed to 5.80 percent from 5.85 percent.
The Dormitory Authority late announced plans to sell $910 million of bonds on October 30 and $281 million of bonds on November 19.

On the competitive side, Goldman Sachs & Co won $200 million Massachusetts Bay Transportation Authority general transportation system bonds with a true interest cost of 5.674 percent. Bonds in the top 2026 maturity were reoffered at a 5.75 percent yield.
